claims.hypothesis: Does high-velocity HCN 3-2 emission along the minor axis trace an outflow, and how does it relate to the OHM structure?
claims.experiment: Position-velocity diagram and high-velocity integrated intensity maps of the ALMA HCN 3-2 cube along the minor axis, compared with e-MERLIN OHM maps
claims.result: High-velocity emission (>200 km/s out to ~600 km/s) is linear and confined along PA ~105 deg, redshifted SE and blueshifted NW
claims.finding: HCN traces a fast collimated outflow enveloped by a wide-angle slow outflow traced by the OHM

evidence.quote: We propose that the high-velocity HCN emission traces a fast ($>250$ km s$^{-1}$) and collimated outflow, that is enveloped by a wide-angle and slow ($\sim 50$ km s$^{-1}$) outflow that is traced by the OHM emission.

claims.hypothesis: Will the slow wide-angle OHM outflow escape the nuclear region?
claims.experiment: Estimated OHM outflow mass and velocity, compared with escape velocity and integrated radiative acceleration numerically
claims.result: v ~ 50 km/s versus sqrt(2) v_circ ~ 200 km/s; infall after ~4e5 yr in the integration
claims.finding: The OHM outflow falls back as a fountain flow while the HCN outflow escapes the nuclear region

evidence.quote: Analysis of the outflow kinematics suggests that the slow wide-angle outflow will not reach escape velocity and instead will fall back to the galaxy disk, evolving as a so-called fountain flow

claims.hypothesis: Can the collimated HCN outflow be launched by momentum-conserving radiation pressure?
claims.experiment: Derived HCN outflow mass and momentum flux and compared with L_IR/c
claims.result: pdot_HCN/(L_IR/c) ~ 7-34, much higher than the OHM outflow
claims.finding: Radiation pressure alone is hard to reconcile with the HCN outflow; an extra momentum boost is needed

evidence.quote: Thus, without a significant momentum boost, it is difficult to explain the collimated HCN outflow with a momentum conserving outflow launching mechanism.

claims.hypothesis: Why is OHM emission absent in the nuclear region while H2CO megamaser emission is present?
claims.experiment: Compared e-MERLIN OH and H2CO maps with published excitation modeling
claims.result: H2CO megamaser traces the nuclear disk; OHM appears only in the outflow and not in the nucleus
claims.finding: High densities in the nuclear region suppress the OH maser, so OH and H2CO megamasers arise from different structures

evidence.quote: We suggest that the absence of OH emission or absorption around $1.67$ GHz in the nuclear disk is the consequence of the high densities in these regions

referee_caveats_inferred: Key ALMA kinematic results rest on a by-eye p-v ellipse and by-eye velocity cuts with no uncertainties or fitting.
Outflow mass uses a HCN 1-0 dense-gas conversion with an assumed 0.3 line ratio, and only the red wing; mass-loss rates span a factor of ~6 without a stated error budget.
Outflow velocity (250 km/s) and size (30 pc) are adopted rather than measured, and no inclination correction is described.
The text gives both ~4e5 yr and ~1 Myr for the OHM fountain timescale.
Possible HCN absorption and line blending (CH2NH, HCO+ and vibrational HCN neighbours) in the HCN window are not modelled.
